task.name: Audit redaction removes numeric usage counts, so per-token cost cannot be derived from any record
task.story_text:
## Observed

Per-invocation usage counts are recorded and then removed by the audit scrubber. In
`cost.agents[].model_usage[]`, the `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, and
`cache_creation_tokens` fields are all written as `[REDACTED]` while the sibling `cost_usd` and
`model` fields survive.

The scrubber's key pattern matches any key containing `token`, which is intended to catch
credential-bearing keys but also matches every usage-count key. 575 of 1041 stored records contain
the redaction marker.

The consequence is that observed cost cannot be normalised. A record carries what an invocation
cost but not what it bought, so cost per unit of work is not derivable from the substrate for any
run, and any consumer wanting a rate has to fall back on declared figures.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** numeric usage counts are stored as the literal string `[REDACTED]` in
  audit records, while cost and model identity on the same object are retained.
- **Evidence:** `src/theforge/coordinator/redact.py:22` defines
  `_SECRET_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)(secret|token|password|api[_-]?key|authorization)")`; the
  `token` alternative matches `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, and
  `cache_creation_tokens`.
- **Ruled out:** not a writer-side omission — the renderer emits the counts, and they are present
  on the object until the scrubber runs.
- **Confirmed cause:** the secret-key pattern classifies by substring rather than by whether the
  value could carry a credential, so a numeric telemetry count keyed with the word token is
  treated identically to a bearer credential.
- **Affected code path:** `coordinator.redact` applied to the `model_usage` entries built by
  `coordinator.audit_render`.
- **Fix-success criterion:** numeric usage counts survive redaction while credential-bearing
  fields continue to be removed, and a future widening of the key pattern that would re-capture
  telemetry is caught rather than silently discarding it again.

Recovery is forward-only. The 575 affected records are immutable and the original counts are not
recorded anywhere else, so no reindex or migration restores them; only runs after the fix carry
usable counts.

## Expected

Redaction should distinguish values that can carry a credential from values that cannot. A field
holding a bounded numeric measurement is telemetry regardless of the word used to name it, and
removing it costs evidence while protecting nothing. Because the scrubber is a trust boundary, a
narrowing of it should be explicit and guarded, so that the reason a particular class of field is
retained survives later edits to the pattern rather than being reverted by the next person
widening it.

handoff.summary: Fixed audit redaction destroying numeric usage counts. The scrubber classified by key name alone, so input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_read_tokens/cache_creation_tokens were replaced with '[REDACTED]' identically to real credentials. Added _carries_no_credential() to redact.py: a credential is always a string, so int/float values on secret-shaped keys are retained while string values on those same keys are still scrubbed; None, dicts, and lists on secret keys keep the old scrubbing behaviour. Because this narrows a trust boundary, the carve-out is guarded mechanically rather than by comment — TELEMETRY_NUMERIC_KEYS is an exported registry of the four audit usage-count keys (mirroring the existing ROUTING_SYMMETRY_REGISTRY pattern in this subsystem), and parametrised tests over it assert each key survives with a numeric value and is still redacted with a string value, so a future widening of _SECRET_KEY_RE fails a test instead of silently discarding telemetry. Added a render-to-redact seam test driving real audit_render._model_usage_entries output through redact() with a live .env credential present, asserting counts and cost survive (cost per unit of work is derivable) while the credential is scrubbed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Numeric usage counts survive redaction while credential-bearing fields continue to be removed
acceptance_criteria.notes: _redact_obj skips redaction when the value is int/float. Verified by TestRedactNumericTelemetry (numeric survives, string on the same key still scrubbed, api_key/authorization/password unaffected) and TestRedactAuditRenderSeam (real _model_usage_entries output keeps all four counts plus cost_usd and model while a .env credential in a sibling field is scrubbed). All 8 pre-existing TestRedactSecretKeys tests still pass unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A future widening of the key pattern that would re-capture telemetry is caught rather than silently discarding it again
acceptance_criteria.notes: TELEMETRY_NUMERIC_KEYS catalogues the dependent audit keys; two parametrised tests iterate it, so widening _SECRET_KEY_RE or removing the numeric carve-out fails those tests. Module docstring records the rationale so it survives later edits.

deferred_items: Forward-only by design (per spec): the 575 already-stored records are immutable and the original counts exist nowhere else, so no migration or reindex was attempted.

17 full-suite failures in test_cut_rc_isolation.py / test_sprint_lock.py / test_sprint_reexec_collision.py are environmental — multiprocessing semaphore creation raises PermissionError [Errno 1] under the dev sandbox. Unrelated to redaction; none of those files import redact. Expect them to pass in the coordinator's out-of-sandbox gate.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
